newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday with fund demand increasing due to a new domestic A share issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 6.95 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 4.31 million lots from 1.14 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Taiyuan Steel Jade Co, an A share firm, issued 49.5 million shares on the Shenzhen bourse on Monday.
"The issue fanned short-term fund demand by institutions wanting to buy the new shares," a trader said.
Heavy institutional borrowing was seen on Friday, pushing up both volume and the repo rates, in particular those for the early-maturing contracts, traders said.
Traders said they expected the rates to rise further in the next few days due to a large number of new A shares issues on the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down across the board on Monday on a technical correction led by the two late-maturing contracts, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, the latest-maturing contract on the market, fell to 111.84 yuan from 112.18 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 752,329 lots from 524,958 lots.
"The technical correction on Friday had been expected after sharp rises in the past few trading days," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the contracts to consolidate in the next few days.
